# A2UISurface

Shows the UI an agent composed in A2UI, with Ouro HX. Every button is one of your app's declared actions: read and write run, a consequential one asks the person to confirm what the agent prepared, and a person-only one takes them to your app's own screen. Messages that fail core's validator show a short alert, and `onProblems` gets the details for the agent.

```tsx
import { A2UISurface } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/a2ui-surface/a2ui-surface";
```

## Example

```tsx
<A2UISurface
  catalog={recipeCatalog}
  messages={messages}
  onAction={(message) => callTool(message.action.name, message.action.context)}
  onHandoff={({ action }) => navigate(`/recipes/${id}?do=${action}`)}
/>
```

## Use instead when

- Use HX's components directly instead when your own code, not an agent, decides the layout.

## Props

Type: `A2UISurfaceProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `catalog` (required) | `unknown` |  | The app's A2UI catalog, generated from its actions by core's `ouro-a2ui-catalog.mts catalog`. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, width (`max-w-md`). |
| `messages` (required) | `readonly unknown[]` |  | The agent's A2UI v1.0 messages, in order. The surface shows where they leave it. |
| `onAction` (required) | `(message: A2UIActionMessage) => void \| Promise<void>` |  | Runs a pressed read or write button, and a consequential one once the person confirms. Send the message to the agent, or call the action's own tool with `message.action.context`. Return a promise to show the button loading until it settles. |
| `onHandoff` (required) | `(handoff: A2UIHandoff) => void` |  | A person-only button never runs from composed UI: take the person to your app's own screen for it. |
| `onProblems` | `((problems: readonly A2UIProblem[]) => void)` |  | The validator's problems, when the messages fail it; the person sees a short alert instead. Hand them to the agent to correct. |
| `surfaceId` | `string` | the first one the messages create | Which surface to show. |

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `onPress`: Not a prop. A pressed button calls `onAction`, or `onHandoff` for a person-only one: `<A2UISurface onAction={send} onHandoff={openApp}>`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`).

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Types

### `A2UIActionMessage`

The A2UI `action` message a pressed button sends: named after the action's id, with the prepared input as its context.

```ts
interface A2UIActionMessage {
  version: string;
  action: {
    /** The action's id, which is also its MCP tool's name. */
    name: string;
    surfaceId: string;
    sourceComponentId: string;
    timestamp: string;
    /** The button's label, as the person read it. */
    userMessage: string;
    /** The input the agent prepared, by field name. */
    context: Record<string, unknown>;
    /** That the person pressed it, its consent class, and for a consequential action that the person confirmed. */
    metadata: { extensions: { bot_ouroboros_action: { consent: string; by: "person"; confirmed?: true } } };
  };
}
```

### `A2UIHandoff`

Where a person-only button takes the person: the action's id and the declaration's `how`.

```ts
interface A2UIHandoff {
  action: string;
  how: string;
}
```

### `A2UIProblem`

A problem the validator found in the agent's messages, in A2UI's validation error format.

```ts
type A2UIProblem = Problem;
```
